[33m#S1[0m Add microsecond support to ms() with units us, µs, microsecond, and microseconds, so ms("500us") returns 0.5; update unit types, README unit list, and add tests. (Nov 3, 10:35 AM)


[34mInvestigated:[0m Mapped the unit-handling structure of src/index.ts (unit constants, string-literal unit types, the parse regex, and the exhaustive switch) and the README unit documentation. Reviewed the existing parse tests in src/parse.test.ts.

[33mLearned:[0m Units are defined as string-literal union types that feed both the Unit union and StringValue. The parse() regex must include each new alias or it won't match. The switch uses a `satisfies never` default, so a new unit type without a matching case fails type-checking. The milliseconds branch returns the raw value, so microseconds need division by 1000. The README lists units in a type block that must stay in sync with the code.

[32mCompleted:[0m Added a Microseconds type to src/index.ts and included it in the Unit union. Extended the parse regex and switch so microsecond aliases return n / 1000. Added Microseconds to the README type block. Added a "should convert microseconds to ms" test in src/parse.test.ts covering us, µs, μs, microsecond(s), a space before the unit, upper and mixed case, a fractional value, and a negative value. The type-check passes, and the full Jest suite passes with 168 of 168 tests and 100% coverage. The diff touches 3 files with 22 insertions and 3 deletions.

[35mNext Steps:[0m The observed session has reported the work as complete and is awaiting further requests. Any follow-up would be a new request, not ongoing edits.

[36mNotes:[0m The observed session also accepted the μs spelling (Greek mu, U+03BC) alongside the µs micro sign (U+00B5), which was not in the original request. Formatting was intentionally left unchanged, so ms(0.5) still returns "0.5ms". The README prose section on fractional values was not reported as updated; only the type block was.
